title.english: Asma bint al-Nu'man ibn al-Harith ibn Sharahil [1]

segments.arabic:
١٠٨١٥- أسماء بنت النعمان بن الحارث
بن شراحيل «١»، وقيل بنت النعمان بن الأسود بن الحارث بن شراحيل الكندية. قال أبو عمر: أجمعوا أنّ رسول اللَّه ﷺ تزوّجها، واختلفوا في قصة فراقها إلى أن قال:
قال قتادة: هي أسماء بنت النعمان، من بني الحارث لما أدخلت عليه دعاها، فقالت: تعال أنت، وأبت أن تجيء. قال قتادة: وقيل إنها قالت له: أعوذ باللَّه منك. فقال: «قد عذت بمعاذ» .
وهذا باطل، إنما قالت: هذه امرأة أخرى من بني سليم.
وقال أبو عبيدة: كلتاهما عاذتا باللَّه منه، وقال غيره: المستعيذة امرأة من بني العنبر من سبي ذات الشقوق، وكانت جميلة، فخاف نساؤه أن تغلبهن عليه.
وقال عبد اللَّه بن محمّد بن عقيل الكندية: هي الشقية التي سألت رسول اللَّه ﷺ أن يفارقها ويردّها إلى قومها، ففعل فردّها مع أبي أسيد.
وقال آخرون: كانت أسماء بنت النعمان الكندية من أجمل النساء، فخاف نساؤه أن تغلبهنّ عليه، فقلن لها: إنّه يحبّ إذا دنا منك أن تقولي أعوذ باللَّه منك، ففعلت، وكانت تسمي نفسها شقية.
وزاد الجرجانيّ: فخلف عليها المهاجر بن أبي أمية المخزومي، ثم قيس بن مكشوح المرادي.
قال أبو عمر: سماها بعضهم أميمة بنت النعمان، وبعضهم أمامة، والاختلاف في الكندية كثير جدا، والاضطراب فيها وفي صواحبها اللاتي لم يدخل بهنّ كثير.
قلت: ونسبها محمد بن حبيب في فصل النساء اللاتي لم يدخل بهنّ ﷺ مثل القول الثاني المذكور أولا، وقال: كانت من أجمل النساء وأشبهن. وذكر قصة النساء معها وفراقها، وأن المهاجر تزوّجها ثم قيس بن مكشوح، ثم قال: والجونية امرأة من كندة أيضا أحضرها أبو أسيد الساعدي، فتولّت عائشة وحفصة أمرها، فقالت لها إحداهما: إنه يعجبه إذا دخلت عليه المرأة أن تقول: أعوذ باللَّه منك ... القصة.
قلت:
والّذي في صحيح البخاريّ في الجونية من طريق الأوزاعي، سألت الزهري: أي أزواج النبي ﷺ استعاذت منه؟ قال: أخبرني عروة، عن عائشة- أن ابنة الجون لما دخلت على رسول اللَّه ﷺ ودنا منها، قالت: أعوذ باللَّه منك. قال: «لقد عذت بعظيم، الحقي بأهلك» .
(١) أسد الغابة: ت ٦٧١٦، الاستيعاب: ت ٣٢٧٧.
segments.english:
10815—Asma bint al-Nu'man ibn al-Harith ibn Sharahil [1]

It is also said: bint al-Nu'man ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Harith ibn Sharahil, the Kindite. Abu Umar said: They unanimously agreed that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, married her, but they differed concerning the account of his separation from her. He continued until he said:

Qatada said: She was Asma bint al-Nu'man, of Banu al-Harith. When she was brought in to him, he called her, but she said, “You come here,” and refused to come. Qatada said: It is also said that she told him, “I seek refuge in Allah from you.” He replied, “You have indeed sought refuge in a refuge-giver.”

This is false. The woman who said that was another woman, from Banu Sulaym.

Abu Ubayda said: Both women sought refuge in Allah from him. Someone else said: The woman who sought refuge was a woman of Banu al-Anbar, among the captives of Dhat al-Shuquq. She was beautiful, so his wives feared that she would prevail over them in his affection.

Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil said concerning the Kindite woman: She was the ill-fated woman who asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to separate from her and return her to her people. He did so and sent her back with Abu Usayd.

Others said: Asma bint al-Nu'man al-Kindiyya was one of the most beautiful women. His wives feared that she would prevail over them in his affection, so they told her, “When he draws near to you, he likes you to say, ‘I seek refuge in Allah from you.’” She did so, and she used to call herself “the ill-fated one.”

Al-Jurjani added: Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya al-Makhzumi subsequently married her, and then Qays ibn Makshuh al-Muradi.

Abu Umar said: Some called her Umayma bint al-Nu'man, and others Umama. The disagreement concerning the Kindite woman is exceedingly extensive, as is the confusion concerning her and the other women with whom he did not consummate marriage.

I say: In the section on the women with whom he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not consummate marriage, Muhammad ibn Habib gave her lineage according to the second opinion mentioned at the outset. He said: She was among the most beautiful women and among those most closely resembling them. He related the account of the women’s dealings with her, his separation from her, and al-Muhajir’s marriage to her, followed by that of Qays ibn Makshuh. He then said: “The Jawniyya was another woman from Kinda. Abu Usayd al-Sa'idi brought her, and Aisha and Hafsa took charge of her affairs. One of them told her, ‘When a woman comes in to him, he likes her to say, “I seek refuge in Allah from you”’”—and the rest of the account.

I say:

What appears in Sahih al-Bukhari concerning the Jawniyya, through al-Awza'i, is: “I asked al-Zuhri, ‘Which of the wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sought refuge from him?’ He said: ‘Urwa informed me, from Aisha, that when the daughter of al-Jawn entered upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he drew near to her, she said, “I seek refuge in Allah from you.” He said, “You have indeed sought refuge in a Mighty One. Rejoin your family.”’”

[1] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 6716; al-Isti'ab, entry 3277.

segments.arabic:
وأخرج من طريق حمزة ابن أبي أسيد عن أبي سيد، قال: خرجنا مع رسول اللَّه ﷺ حتى انطلقنا إلى حائط يقال لها الشوط، فقال: «اجلسوا ها هنا، فدخل وقد أتى بالجونيّة، فأنزلت في بيت علي ومعها دايتها. فلما دخل عليها قال: «هبي لي نفسك» . قال: قالت:
هل تهب الملكة نفسها للسّوقة! قال: فأهوى بيده ليضعها عليها لتسكن. قالت: أعوذ باللَّه منك. قال: «لقد عذت بمعاذ» .
ثم أخرج الحديث.
وأخرج ابن سعد، من طرق عدة كلّها عن الواقدي- أنّ الجونية استعاذت من النبي ﷺ. واختلف: هل هي بنت النعمان أو أخته؟ وسماها عن عبد اللَّه بن جعفر المخزومي أمية.
وأخرج ابن سعد، عن هشام بن محمد، وهو ابن الكلبي، عن ابن الغسيل الّذي أخرجه البخاري، وزاد فيه: فقالت حفصة لعائشة أو عائشة لحفصة: اخضبيها وأنا أمشطها، ففعلتها، ثم قالت لها إحداهما: إنه يعجبه من المرأة إذا دخلت عليه أن تقول: أعوذ باللَّه منك، فلما دخلت عليه وأغلق الباب وأرخى الستر مدّ يده إليها، فقالت: أعوذ باللَّه منك، فقال بكمه على وجهه، وقال: «عذت معاذا» - ثلاث مرات، ثم أخرج علي، فقال: «يا أبا أسيد، ألحقها، بأهلها ومتّعها برازقيّتين» «١» يعني كرباسين «٢»، فكانت تقول: ادعوني الشقية.
ومن طريق عمر بن الحكم عن أبي أسيد في هذه القصة، فقلت: يا رسول اللَّه، قد جئتك بأهلك، فخرج يمشي وأنا معه، فلما أتاها أقعى وأهوى ليقبلها، وكان يفعل ذلك إذا اختلى النساء، فقالت: أعوذ باللَّه منك ... الحديث.
وفيه موسى بن عبيدة، وهو ضعيف.
ومن طريق عباس بن سهل، عن أبي أسيد، قال: لما طلعت بها على قومها تصايحوا، وقالوا: إنك لغير مباركة، لقد جعلتنا في العرب شهرة، فما دهاك؟ قالت: خدعت. فقالت لأبي أسيد: ما أصنع. قال: أقيمي في بيتك واحتجبي إلا من ذي رحم محرم، ولا يطمع فيك أحد، فأقامت كذلك حتى توفيت في خلافة عثمان.
وعن ابن الكلبيّ، عن أبيه، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس: تزوّج رسول اللَّه ﷺ أسماء بنت النعمان، وكانت من أجمل أهل زمانها، وأشبهنّ، فقالت عائشة: قد وضع يده في العراب يوشك أن يصرفن وجهه عنا، وكان خطبها حين وفد أبوها عليه في وفد كندة،
(١) الرّزاقيّة: ثياب كتّان بيض. النهاية ٢/ ٢١٩.
(٢) الكرباس: القطن. النهاية ٤/ ١٦١.
segments.english:
He also transmitted by way of Hamza ibn Abi Usayd, from Abu Usayd, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, until we came to a walled garden called al-Shawt. He said, “Sit here.” He then entered. Al-Jawniyya had been brought and lodged in Ali's house, accompanied by her nurse. When he entered upon her, he said, “Give yourself to me.” She said, “Does a queen give herself to a commoner!” He reached out his hand to place it upon her so that she might become calm. She said, “I seek refuge in Allah from you.” He said, “You have indeed sought refuge with One who grants refuge.”

Then he transmitted the hadith.

Ibn Sa'd transmitted through several routes, all of them from al-Waqidi, that al-Jawniyya sought refuge from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. There was disagreement as to whether she was al-Nu'man's daughter or his sister. In a report from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Makhzumi, he named her Umayya.

Ibn Sa'd also transmitted from Hisham ibn Muhammad—that is, Ibn al-Kalbi—from Ibn al-Ghasil the report that al-Bukhari had transmitted, adding to it: Hafsa said to Aisha, or Aisha said to Hafsa, “Dye her with henna, and I shall comb her hair.” She did so. One of them then said to her, “When a woman enters upon him, he likes her to say, ‘I seek refuge in Allah from you.’” When she entered upon him, and he closed the door, lowered the curtain, and extended his hand toward her, she said, “I seek refuge in Allah from you.” He drew his sleeve over his face and said, “You have indeed sought refuge”—three times. He then came out to me and said, “Abu Usayd, take her back to her family and give her two Raziqi garments as a parting gift,”(1) meaning two pieces of karbas cloth.(2) Thereafter she would say, “Call me the wretched woman.”

Through Umar ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Usayd, concerning this account: I said, “Messenger of Allah, I have brought your wife to you.” He went out walking, and I was with him. When he reached her, he squatted down and leaned toward her to kiss her; he used to do that when he was alone with women. She said, “I seek refuge in Allah from you” ... the hadith.

In its chain is Musa ibn Ubayda, who is weak.

Through Abbas ibn Sahl, from Abu Usayd, who said: When I brought her back to her people, they raised an outcry and said, “You are indeed not blessed! You have made us notorious among the Arabs. What befell you?” She said, “I was deceived.” She then said to Abu Usayd, “What should I do?” He said, “Remain in your house and veil yourself from everyone except an unmarriageable blood relative. Let no one entertain hopes concerning you.” She remained thus until she died during the caliphate of Uthman.

And from Ibn al-Kalbi, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, married Asma bint al-Nu'man. She was one of the most beautiful women of her time and among the youngest of them. Aisha said, “He has turned his attention to women from outside our people; they may soon turn his face away from us.” He had proposed to her when her father came to him with the delegation of Kinda,

(1) Raziqiyya: white linen garments. Al-Nihaya, 2/219.

(2) Karbas: cotton. Al-Nihaya, 4/161.

segments.arabic:
فلما رآها نساؤه حسدنها، فقلن لها: إن أردت أن تحظى عنده ... القصة.
وبه إلى ابن عباس، قال: خلف على أسماء بنت النعمان المهاجر بن أبي أمية، فأراد عمر أن يعاقبها، فقالت: واللَّه ما ضرب على حجاب ولا سمّيت بأم المؤمنين، فكفّ عنها.
وعن الواقديّ: قد بلغني أنّ عكرمة بن أبي جهل تزوّجها في زمن الردة، وليس ذلك بثبت.
وقد ساق ابن سعد قصة الجونية، ومن طريق سعيد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبزى لم يستعذ منه غير الجونية عن الواقدي بسنده مطولة. وتقدم نقلها في ترجمة النعمان بن أبي الجون، وفي آخرها: إن ذلك كان في ربيع الأول سنة تسع من الهجرة.
segments.english:
When his wives saw her, they became jealous of her and said to her, “If you wish to find favor with him ...”—and so the story continues.

Through the same chain to Ibn Abbas, who said: al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya married Asma bint al-Nu'man after the Prophet, and Umar intended to punish her. She said, “By Allah, no veil was ever drawn around me, nor was I called Mother of the Believers.” So he refrained from punishing her.

From al-Waqidi: “I have heard that Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl married her during the time of the Ridda, but that is not established.”

Ibn Sa'd related at length, from al-Waqidi through his chain, the story of al-Jawniyya; and by way of Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza came the report: “No one other than al-Jawniyya sought refuge from him.” That account was quoted previously in the entry on al-Nu'man ibn Abi al-Jawn. At its end it states that this occurred in Rabi' al-Awwal of the ninth year of the Hijra.
